proof_boundary: Roundtable was live but advisory. The manifest is not implementation proof; each slice requires its listed local deterministic acceptance checks.

slices.target: Document and prove source-to-build-to-interaction path for skills/battle/spectator on agent-skills@main.
commands: npm install or existing project install command in skills/battle/spectator if required
static serve freshly built dist on declared Battle port
$test-interactions manifest against the declared Battle URL
slices.acceptance_check: Freshly built artifact from source passes 12/12 interactions with 0 failures and 0 warnings; inspected screenshot visibly shows Battle, not SPARTA or a stale route.
slices.proof_boundary: Proves local source-to-artifact-to-interaction parity only; does not prove live backend data, long-running campaigns, or production deployment.
slices.human_input: Only required if Battle must own port 3002 instead of a dedicated Battle port.

slices.acceptance_check: Backend eval reports 14/14 without relying on an orphaned waiver, or sanity prints an explicit ticket reference and expiry if the human defers the fix.
slices.proof_boundary: Proves the backend fixture validates; does not prove Pixi visual replay correctness.

slices.target: Add a flagged backend/SSE or recorded stream path into the normalized Battle adapter.
commands: record live or local backend stream for a known scenario
replay recorded stream through normalized adapter
compare normalized adapter output byte-for-byte against fixture output
slices.acceptance_check: Recorded live-stream normalized output is byte-identical to fixture output for the same scenario; UI interaction proof passes on fresh receipts.
slices.proof_boundary: Proves transport equivalence for recorded input only; not provider reliability or deployment-scale uptime.

slices.target: Make the backend/Pixi boundary executable by rejecting renderer vocabulary in backend payloads.
slices.acceptance_check: Scanner fails on a deliberately poisoned payload and passes on current Battle backend payloads.
slices.proof_boundary: Proves absence of the listed renderer terms only, not general semantic purity.

slices.target: Prove missing/invalid receipts suppress Pixi effects while DOM mirrors remain accessible and disabled.
commands: $test-interactions manifest for disabled DOM mirror states
slices.acceptance_check: Terminal effects are suppressed; DOM mirrors remain present with data-qid, data-qs-action, title, aria-label, keyboard focus behavior, and correct disabled state.
slices.proof_boundary: Proves the seeded fail-closed cases only.

slices.target: Enumerate selectable lanes, markers, and outcomes from adapter output and diff them against DOM data-qid mirrors.
slices.acceptance_check: Every selectable adapter item has exactly one DOM mirror with data-qid, data-qs-action, title, aria-label, and keyboard focus behavior.
slices.proof_boundary: Proves coverage parity, not semantic click correctness.

slices.target: Exercise SSE/live-client behavior for reconnect, duplicate delivery, ordering, stale receipts, malformed events, and backend restart.
slices.acceptance_check: Accepted effects occur once; duplicate or stale events do not replay terminal effects; malformed semantic payloads fail closed with recorded receipts.
slices.proof_boundary: Proves the injected transport fault cases only, not real-provider uptime.

slices.target: Package a clean-checkout Battle frontend/backend smoke that does not rely on existing developer processes.
commands: clean checkout or clean worktree package command
slices.acceptance_check: Battle frontend loads through the declared route; backend health identifies Battle; fresh campaign, interaction suite, and screenshot capture pass without relying on a pre-existing developer server.
slices.proof_boundary: Proves reproducible local packaging only; not always-on production service or SLO.

human_questions.question: Should Battle claim port 3002, currently used by SPARTA Explorer, or use a dedicated declared Battle port for local proof?
If battle-004 is not repaired immediately, what issue/ticket should own the waiver and expiry?
Are real provider-backed long-running Battle campaigns authorized for the next phase, and under what cost/rate limits?
